391.h: The Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo (FUSTKABO) is a federal university created by an Act of the National Assembly by upgrading the former Federal Polytechnic, Kabo. The National Universities Commission, which licenses and regulates it, records its establishment in 2025. It was set up to widen access to science-led higher education that prepares graduates for employment.
391.a: Students are admitted through JAMB's UTME and by direct entry. The university offers science and technology programmes, and its doctoral study is full-time by regulation.
391.c: It is located in Kabo local government area, Kano State.

393.h: Caleb University is a private university founded by Dr Oladega Adelowo Adebogun, who wanted to produce graduates known for character as well as professional competence. It was one of the private universities licensed to complement public institutions. The National Universities Commission granted its operating licence on 17 May 2007, teaching began in January 2008, and the first matriculation ceremony followed in February 2008.
393.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
393.c: It began on a take-off site at Ikosi GRA, off CMD Road in Lagos, and later moved to its permanent campus at Imota, near Ikorodu, in Lagos State.

401.h: Hezekiah University is a private university founded by Living Christ Mission, and Imo State's first private university. Its founder first approached the National Universities Commission about a university for Imo State in 2004, and the Federal Government licensed it in May 2015. The university's founding idea is that a degree should form character as well as intellect, and it has a zero-tolerance policy on cultism and drug abuse.
401.a: The university offers a range of undergraduate programmes and is accredited by the National Universities Commission. Every student studies on a scholarship provided by the founder.
401.c: It is located in Umudi, in the Nkwerre area of Imo State.

402.h: Michael and Cecilia Ibru University (MCIU) is a private university founded by the industrialist Michael Ibru and his wife, Cecilia Ibru, as the first major project of their Michael and Cecilia Foundation. The Federal Government approved it on 5 March 2015, and teaching began in the 2015/2016 session.
402.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and aims to produce graduates who can compete internationally. It is one of the institutions supporting the AltSchool Africa programme, which trains software engineers across the continent.
402.c: The campus is at Agbarha-Otor, Delta State.

403.h: KolaDaisi University (KDU) is a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission in November 2016, after approval by the Federal Executive Council. It was founded by Chief Kola Daisi, the Bashorun of Ibadan, and its proprietor is the Kola Daisi Foundation, which he set up in 1993. The foundation had supported education for years before the university, through donations to Nigerian universities, endowed prizes and scholarships.
403.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes with an emphasis on graduate employability.
403.c: It is located in Ibadan, Oyo State.

407.h: Clifford University is a private Christian, co-educational university owned and run by the Seventh-day Adventist Church in Nigeria, one of about 144 tertiary institutions the church operates worldwide. It is named after Jesse Clifford and his wife, English missionaries who brought the Adventist message to eastern Nigeria. Sent to West Africa in 1905, they worked in Sierra Leone and Ghana, reached Abua in Rivers State in 1920, and moved to Aba in 1923. The National Universities Commission records the university's establishment in 2016.
407.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and aims to develop students intellectually, professionally, physically, socially and spiritually.
407.c: The campus is at Ihie, near Owerrinta, in Abia State.

409.h: Atiba University is a private university established in December 2017. It is named after Alaafin Atiba, a nineteenth-century ruler of the Oyo kingdom.
409.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes, including a Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences. Its fees are relatively low and can be paid in up to three instalments a year.
409.c: It is located in Oyo town, Oyo State.

419.h: Havilla University (HUNI) is a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission on 8 April 2021. Its founder, Blessing Tangban, established it to fill a gap in university education in the northern and central senatorial districts of Cross River State.
419.a: The university has four faculties, Computing and Sciences, Management and Social Sciences, Law, and Health Sciences, offering 16 approved programmes. It admits students regardless of race, colour, nationality or ethnic origin.
419.c: The campus covers 228 hectares at kilometre 15 on the Ikom-Ogoja road, near Ikom. It is about 215 kilometres from Calabar, 84 kilometres from Ogoja, 100 kilometres from Abakaliki and just 28 kilometres from the border with Cameroon.

421.h: James Hope University (JHU) is a private university founded by Jim Ovia, the founder of Zenith Bank, through his non-profit foundation. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2021. In January 2024 it launched a business school, developed through partnerships with international academic institutions.
421.a: The university offers postgraduate programmes that combine academic theory with practical application, all approved by the National Universities Commission, with a particular focus on business and professional education.
421.c: It is located in Lekki, Lagos.
